Based on the AKC ranking data from 2013-2024, here are the dog breeds that **consistently** appeared in the top 10 every single year during that period:

## Breeds in the Top 10 Every Year (2013-2024):

| Breed | Years in Top 10 | Notes |
|-------|----------------|-------|
| **Labrador Retriever** | All 12 years | #1 for 31 consecutive years overall; held #1 through 2021, then dropped to #2 in 2022-2024 |
| **Golden Retriever** | All 12 years | Generally ranked #3, briefly #4 in 2020 |
| **German Shepherd** | All 12 years | Ranked #2 through 2019, then #3 in 2020, #4 from 2021-2024 |
| **Beagle** | All 12 years | Started at #4 in 2013, gradually declined to #7 by 2024 |
| **Bulldog** | All 12 years | High rankings (#4-#5) early in the period, then declined to #7-#9 later |
| **Rottweiler** | All 12 years | Very consistent, oscillating between #7-#10 |
| **French Bulldog** | 10 of 12 years (NOT 2013-2014) | Entered top 10 at #9 in 2014, climbed to #1 by 2022 |
| **Poodle** | 10 of 12 years (NOT 2013-2014... wait, actually was there?) | Was #8 and #7 consistently, moved into top 5 starting 2018 |

Wait, let me reconsider. Looking at the data more carefully:

- **French Bulldog**: Ranked #11 in 2013, #9 in 2014 → **missed 2013**
- **Poodle**: Ranked #8 in 2013 → **was in top 10**

So the truly **consistent** breeds (all 12 years from 2013-2024):

| # | Breed |
|---|-------|
| 1 | **Labrador Retriever** |
| 2 | **Golden Retriever** |
| 3 | **German Shepherd** |
| 4 | **Beagle** |

**Dachshund** was #10 in 2013 and stayed in top 10 every year after (dropping out momentarily? No, looking again: #10 in 2013, #11 in 2014... so Dachshund missed 2014).

### Breeds Consistently in Top 10 (2013-2024):

1. **Labrador Retriever** ✓

**Answer: 7 breeds** — Labrador Retriever, Golden Retriever, German Shepherd, Beagle, Bulldog, Rottweiler, and Poodle — were all in the top 10 every single year from 2013-2024.

**Notable changes:**
- French Bulldog jumped from outside top 10 to #1 by 2022

The French Bulldog is America's most popular dog breed, according to the American Kennel Club's ranking for 2025. It has held No. 1 for four years in a row, ahead of the Labrador Retriever, Golden Retriever, German Shepherd Dog and Dachshund. The Dachshund is the only new face in the top five this year: it moved up one place and pushed the Poodle down to sixth.
The top 10 itself has not gained or lost a breed since 2020. The same ten breeds have been trading places for six years, and those swaps show where owners' tastes are moving. The chart below follows 13 years of AKC rankings, from 2013 to 2025. Tap a breed to follow its line, or tap a year to see that year's top 10.

## **The 2025 top 10, and how each breed moved**
Only two pairs of breeds changed places between 2024 and 2025: the Dachshund and Poodle, and the German Shorthaired Pointer and Bulldog. The other six held their spots. Compared with 2020, the picture is a little different, because the Dachshund and Bulldog have moved five places each in opposite directions.

## **How the French Bulldog went from No. 11 to No. 1**
In 2013 the French Bulldog ranked 11th. By 2017 it was 4th, in 2020 it passed the German Shepherd and the Golden Retriever to reach 2nd, and in 2022 it overtook the Labrador Retriever. The AKC describes that as the end of the Labrador's 31-year run at the top, and reports that French Bulldog registrations have risen by more than 1,000 percent since 2012, when the breed ranked 14th.
A ranking cannot say why people choose a breed. The reasons usually offered are practical ones: a compact body, modest exercise needs, and a size that suits apartments and city life. Popularity brings its own care questions. Flat-faced breeds can struggle in heat and with breathing, so our French Bulldog breathing signs and safety tips Opens in a new window. and our guide on how to keep a French Bulldog cool safely Opens in a new window. are good next reads, along with the French Bulldog lifespan and care guide Opens in a new window..

## **Dachshund up, Bulldog down: the biggest swap in the top 10**
The Dachshund sat at 13th for three years running, from 2015 to 2017. It was back at 10th in 2020, 9th in 2022, jumped to 6th in 2023 and reached 5th in 2025. The Bulldog went the other way. It was 4th from 2014 to 2016, held 5th through 2020, and has slipped in four of the five years since, to 10th in 2025.
The ranking does not say why owners moved. It does show that the shift was gradual: the two breeds changed places over five years, not in one. If you live with a Dachshund, read about Dachshund health risks, including back problems and weight Opens in a new window.. If you are weighing a Bulldog, see our Bulldog temperament guide Opens in a new window..

## **Steady at the top, with one long slide**
*   **Labrador Retriever:** No. 1 every year from 2013 to 2021, No. 2 since 2022. See the Labrador Retriever lifespan and care Opens in a new window..  
*   **Golden Retriever:** 3rd in every year except 2020, when it was 4th. See the Golden Retriever lifespan and care Opens in a new window..  
*   **German Shepherd Dog:** 2nd from 2013 to 2019, 3rd in 2020, and 4th every year since 2021, two places lower than where it started. See the German Shepherd lifespan and care Opens in a new window..  
*   **Poodle:** 8th in 2013, then a climb into the top five from 2021 to 2024. The AKC noted that its 2021 return to the top five was the first since 1997. It is 6th in 2025. See the Poodle lifespan across Toy, Miniature and Standard sizes Opens in a new window..  
*   **Beagle:** 4th in 2013 and 7th in 2025. See the Beagle care and lifespan guide Opens in a new window..  
*   **Rottweiler and German Shorthaired Pointer:** the Rottweiler has stayed between 7th and 10th all 13 years, while the German Shorthaired Pointer climbed from 13th in 2013 to 9th. See the Rottweiler lifespan guide Opens in a new window..

## **Breeds that left the top 10, and who is next**
Three breeds on the chart no longer sit in the top 10. The Yorkshire Terrier was 6th in 2013 and is 13th in 2025. The Boxer went from 7th to 18th. The Pembroke Welsh Corgi came from far back, 24th in 2013, to 10th in 2019, then held 11th for four years before slipping to 15th and then 16th. If you share a home with a Corgi, our Corgi lifespan and care guide Opens in a new window. and Corgi spine safety Opens in a new window. cover the basics.
The next breed to watch is the Cane Corso, which rose from 14th in 2024 to 11th in 2025. The Cavalier King Charles Spaniel (12th), Yorkshire Terrier (13th), Australian Shepherd (14th) and Doberman Pinscher (15th) follow it.

## **What the AKC ranking does and does not measure**
*   It counts registrations with the American Kennel Club, a registry of purebred dogs. Mixed breeds and dogs that are not registered are not part of the list.  
*   Registration is voluntary, so the list compares breeds among registered dogs. It is not a census of every dog in American homes.  
*   A rank shows position, not volume. A breed can fall in rank because others rose past it, and the AKC makes the same point about its own list.  
*   Each ranking covers one calendar year of registrations and is published afterward. In the 2025 ranking, 202 breeds were counted.
Because the AKC pages publish ranks rather than registration counts, this article reports ranks only and does not estimate how many dogs each breed represents.

## **Using popularity when you choose a dog, a bed or anything sized by breed**
A breed being popular says little about whether it suits your home. Size, energy, coat, and common health needs matter more, and they vary within a breed. When you shop for a bed, harness or stairs, use the dog's measurements, not a breed label: our guide to Dog size by measurement, not breed Opens in a new window. shows how, and the Pet Size & Fit Finder Opens in a new window. turns measurements into a size. If a smaller dog is on your list, the best small dog breeds for your home Opens in a new window. is a calm place to start.

## **Most popular dog breeds: common questions**
### What is the most popular dog breed in America?
The French Bulldog, according to the American Kennel Club's ranking for 2025. It has been No. 1 for four years in a row, ahead of the Labrador Retriever, Golden Retriever, German Shepherd Dog and Dachshund.

## **Most popular dog breeds: common questions**
### How long was the Labrador Retriever the most popular breed?
The AKC counted 31 consecutive years at No. 1 before the French Bulldog took the top spot in 2022. In the 13 years charted here, the Labrador was No. 1 from 2013 through 2021 and has been No. 2 since.

## **Most popular dog breeds: common questions**
### Has the AKC top 10 changed recently?
Only in order. The same ten breeds have made up the top 10 every year from 2020 to 2025. The biggest moves were the Dachshund rising from 10th to 5th and the Bulldog falling from 5th to 10th.

## **Most popular dog breeds: common questions**
### Are mixed breeds and doodles in the ranking?
No. The AKC is a registry of purebred dogs and ranks only the breeds it recognizes, so mixed-breed dogs are not counted as a group in this list.

## **Most popular dog breeds: common questions**
### How does the AKC decide the ranking?
It ranks breeds by registration statistics for the calendar year. Registration is voluntary, so the list shows how breeds compare among AKC-registered dogs, not every dog in American homes.

## **Most popular dog breeds: common questions**
### Which breeds have dropped out of the top 10 since 2013?
The Yorkshire Terrier, which was 6th in 2013 and is 13th in 2025, and the Boxer, which fell from 7th to 18th. The Pembroke Welsh Corgi reached 10th in 2019 and is 16th in 2025.

It has held No. 1 for four years in a row, ahead of the Labrador Retriever, Golden Retriever, German Shepherd Dog and Dachshund. The Dachshund is the only new face in the top five this year: it moved up one place and pushed the Poodle down to sixth.
The top 10 itself has not gained or lost a breed since 2020. The same ten breeds have been trading places for six years, and those swaps show where owners' tastes are moving. The chart below follows 13 years of AKC rankings, from 2013 to 2025. Tap a breed to follow its line, or tap a year to see that year's top 10.

## **The 2025 top 10, and how each breed moved**
Only two pairs of breeds changed places between 2024 and 2025: the Dachshund and Poodle, and the German Shorthaired Pointer and Bulldog. The other six held their spots. Compared with 2020, the picture is a little different, because the Dachshund and Bulldog have moved five places each in opposite directions.

## **How the French Bulldog went from No. 11 to No. 1**
In 2013 the French Bulldog ranked 11th. By 2017 it was 4th, in 2020 it passed the German Shepherd and the Golden Retriever to reach 2nd, and in 2022 it overtook the Labrador Retriever. The AKC describes that as the end of the Labrador's 31-year run at the top, and reports that French Bulldog registrations have risen by more than 1,000 percent since 2012, when the breed ranked 14th.
A ranking cannot say why people choose a breed. The reasons usually offered are practical ones: a compact body, modest exercise needs, and a size that suits apartments and city life. Popularity brings its own care questions. Flat-faced breeds can struggle in heat and with breathing, so our French Bulldog breathing signs and safety tips Opens in a new window. and our guide on how to keep a French Bulldog cool safely Opens in a new window. are good next reads, along with the French Bulldog lifespan and care guide Opens in a new window..

## **Dachshund up, Bulldog down: the biggest swap in the top 10**
The Dachshund sat at 13th for three years running, from 2015 to 2017. It was back at 10th in 2020, 9th in 2022, jumped to 6th in 2023 and reached 5th in 2025. The Bulldog went the other way. It was 4th from 2014 to 2016, held 5th through 2020, and has slipped in four of the five years since, to 10th in 2025.
The ranking does not say why owners moved. It does show that the shift was gradual: the two breeds changed places over five years, not in one. If you live with a Dachshund, read about Dachshund health risks, including back problems and weight Opens in a new window.. If you are weighing a Bulldog, see our Bulldog temperament guide Opens in a new window..

## **Steady at the top, with one long slide**
*   **Labrador Retriever:** No. 1 every year from 2013 to 2021, No. 2 since 2022. See the Labrador Retriever lifespan and care Opens in a new window..  
*   **Golden Retriever:** 3rd in every year except 2020, when it was 4th. See the Golden Retriever lifespan and care Opens in a new window..  
*   **German Shepherd Dog:** 2nd from 2013 to 2019, 3rd in 2020, and 4th every year since 2021, two places lower than where it started. See the German Shepherd lifespan and care Opens in a new window..  
*   **Poodle:** 8th in 2013, then a climb into the top five from 2021 to 2024. The AKC noted that its 2021 return to the top five was the first since 1997. It is 6th in 2025. See the Poodle lifespan across Toy, Miniature and Standard sizes Opens in a new window..  
*   **Beagle:** 4th in 2013 and 7th in 2025. See the Beagle care and lifespan guide Opens in a new window..  
*   **Rottweiler and German Shorthaired Pointer:** the Rottweiler has stayed between 7th and 10th all 13 years, while the German Shorthaired Pointer climbed from 13th in 2013 to 9th. See the Rottweiler lifespan guide Opens in a new window..

## **Breeds that left the top 10, and who is next**
Three breeds on the chart no longer sit in the top 10. The Yorkshire Terrier was 6th in 2013 and is 13th in 2025. The Boxer went from 7th to 18th. The Pembroke Welsh Corgi came from far back, 24th in 2013, to 10th in 2019, then held 11th for four years before slipping to 15th and then 16th. If you share a home with a Corgi, our Corgi lifespan and care guide Opens in a new window. and Corgi spine safety Opens in a new window. cover the basics.
The next breed to watch is the Cane Corso, which rose from 14th in 2024 to 11th in 2025. The Cavalier King Charles Spaniel (12th), Yorkshire Terrier (13th), Australian Shepherd (14th) and Doberman Pinscher (15th) follow it.
texts.9:
## **What the AKC ranking does and does not measure**
*   It counts registrations with the American Kennel Club, a registry of purebred dogs. Mixed breeds and dogs that are not registered are not part of the list.  
*   Registration is voluntary, so the list compares breeds among registered dogs. It is not a census of every dog in American homes.  
*   A rank shows position, not volume. A breed can fall in rank because others rose past it, and the AKC makes the same point about its own list.  
*   Each ranking covers one calendar year of registrations and is published afterward. In the 2025 ranking, 202 breeds were counted.
Because the AKC pages publish ranks rather than registration counts, this article reports ranks only and does not estimate how many dogs each breed represents.

## **Using popularity when you choose a dog, a bed or anything sized by breed**
A breed being popular says little about whether it suits your home. Size, energy, coat, and common health needs matter more, and they vary within a breed. When you shop for a bed, harness or stairs, use the dog's measurements, not a breed label: our guide to Dog size by measurement, not breed Opens in a new window. shows how, and the Pet Size & Fit Finder Opens in a new window. turns measurements into a size. If a smaller dog is on your list, the best small dog breeds for your home Opens in a new window. is a calm place to start.

## **Most popular dog breeds: common questions**
### What is the most popular dog breed in America?
The French Bulldog, according to the American Kennel Club's ranking for 2025. It has been No. 1 for four years in a row, ahead of the Labrador Retriever, Golden Retriever, German Shepherd Dog and Dachshund.
texts.12:
## **Most popular dog breeds: common questions**
### How long was the Labrador Retriever the most popular breed?
The AKC counted 31 consecutive years at No. 1 before the French Bulldog took the top spot in 2022. In the 13 years charted here, the Labrador was No. 1 from 2013 through 2021 and has been No. 2 since.
texts.13:
## **Most popular dog breeds: common questions**
### Has the AKC top 10 changed recently?
Only in order. The same ten breeds have made up the top 10 every year from 2020 to 2025. The biggest moves were the Dachshund rising from 10th to 5th and the Bulldog falling from 5th to 10th.
texts.14:
## **Most popular dog breeds: common questions**
### Are mixed breeds and doodles in the ranking?
No. The AKC is a registry of purebred dogs and ranks only the breeds it recognizes, so mixed-breed dogs are not counted as a group in this list.
texts.15:
## **Most popular dog breeds: common questions**
### How does the AKC decide the ranking?
It ranks breeds by registration statistics for the calendar year. Registration is voluntary, so the list shows how breeds compare among AKC-registered dogs, not every dog in American homes.
texts.16:
## **Most popular dog breeds: common questions**
### Which breeds have dropped out of the top 10 since 2013?
The Yorkshire Terrier, which was 6th in 2013 and is 13th in 2025, and the Boxer, which fell from 7th to 18th. The Pembroke Welsh Corgi reached 10th in 2019 and is 16th in 2025.

## **How the French Bulldog went from No. 11 to No. 1**
In 2013 the French Bulldog ranked 11th. By 2017 it was 4th, in 2020 it passed the German Shepherd and the Golden Retriever to reach 2nd, and in 2022 it overtook the Labrador Retriever. The AKC describes that as the end of the Labrador's 31-year run at the top, and reports that French Bulldog registrations have risen by more than 1,000 percent since 2012, when the breed ranked 14th.

The Dachshund sat at 13th for three years running, from 2015 to 2017. It was back at 10th in 2020, 9th in 2022, jumped to 6th in 2023 and reached 5th in 2025. The Bulldog went the other way. It was 4th from 2014 to 2016, held 5th through 2020, and has slipped in four of the five years since, to 10th in 2025.

## **What the AKC ranking does and does not measure**
*   It counts registrations with the American Kennel Club, a registry of purebred dogs. Mixed breeds and dogs that are not registered are not part of the list.  
*   Registration is voluntary, so the list compares breeds among registered dogs. It is not a census of every dog in American homes.  
*   A rank shows position, not volume. A breed can fall in rank because others rose past it, and the AKC makes the same point about its own list.  
*   Each ranking covers one calendar year of registrations and is published afterward. In the 2025 ranking, 202 breeds were counted.
Because the AKC pages publish ranks rather than registration counts, this article reports ranks only and does not estimate how many dogs each breed represents.
